audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rated Levels 1-5 as 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet levelChart both say Ahri. Two layers rendered different answers to who wins each early stage.
audit.why: Ahri's Orb of Deception is 970 range with a true-damage return half and a 7s cooldown; Charm is 975 range. Anivia's only pre-6 answer is an 1075-range Flash Frost on an 11s cooldown at rank 1 that she can walk around. Ahri holds every stage until Glacial Storm.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side set to Ahri to match win[0..4] and the packet chart; ratings dropped to 4/10 for those rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer pinned the first-item spike to Rylai's Crystal Scepter while the full layer's itemization calls for Lost Chapter into Rod of Ages/Seraph's. The two layers named different first items.
audit.why: Anivia's spike is mana and storm uptime, not the Rylai's slow — Glacial Storm already chills, and the chill is what doubles Frostbite. Ahri's own spikes are Charm at 3, Spirit Rush at 6 (140/120/100s), and Essence Theft sustain across the whole laning phase.
audit.corrected: whys[5] and spikes[2].text now describe the mana/first-item spike as storm uptime plus doubled Frostbite rather than a Rylai's purchase.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Crystallize creates impassable terrain and Spirit Rush is a dash, so a wall placed behind Ahri mid-dash denies her exit from Glacial Storm. Also missing: Orb of Deception's return half is true damage (MR is the wrong buy), and Essence Theft heals the chip back.
audit.why: Anivia W flag: 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Ahri R flag: 'dash — mobility that grounding and walls can deny'. Anivia E doubles damage on a target recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm, and E is a 4s cooldown, so the chill lets it double repeatedly.
audit.corrected: Wall-into-storm interaction written into breakdown.carry, breakdown.late, dosFull[1], mid and tradeGood; true damage recorded in early and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns told the player to count Charm without giving a number, and gave the wall and ultimate joke lines instead of cooldowns.
audit.why: Charm is a flat 12s at every rank, Spirit Rush 140/120/100s, Crystallize a flat 17s, Flash Frost 11/10/9/8/7s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer line referred to Ahri as 'he'/'his'.
audit.why: Ahri is female; the enemy kit text uses she/her throughout.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in tldr, winCon, loading, dosFull titles, dontsFull titles, report[0], report[1], report[11].

edits.before: - Ahri Charm: matchup-defining — The charm starts every kill pattern — stay behind minions while it is up. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Crystallize has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Charm is a flat 12s at every rank — it never shortens, so count it and step up the second it is gone. - Spirit Rush is 140/120/100s and it is her only exit once your 17s wall lands behind her. - Flash Frost is 11s at rank 1, so a whiff is her window, not yours.

edits.after: A fed Ahri kills the bird and the egg inside one Charm-Q-R, so hold the minion line between you and let Charm die on a caster. Clear with Glacial Storm and keep the wall for her dive.

edits.before: Level 6 is brutal: Spirit Rush lets Ahri dash in for a Charm-R combo and dash back out before your Glacial Storm even finishes ticking, so you need summoner spells and vision to survive rather than win the lane outright.

edits.before: Ahri's Orb of Deception chip damage plus a Charm threat means you're mostly farming passively under turret through levels 1-5 — she can punish any greedy Flash Frost attempt by simply walking around it, and her range keeps you from ever getting a clean Rebirth-backed trade in.
edits.after: Ahri's Orb of Deception chips you for free and the return half is true damage, so MR does not blunt it, and Essence Theft heals the chip back off nine minions. Farm from behind the line through levels 1-5, spend Flash Frost only on a step-up, and let its 11s cooldown be a threat you never waste.
